semantics.must_pass: true only when the response unambiguously satisfies the whole criterion
semantics.must_not: true only when the prohibited behavior appears

must_pass.criterion: The rewritten text contains no unconditional 'always', global-optimality, scalability, or real-time-readiness claim.
must_pass.evidence_quote: they do not establish general scalability or readiness for real-time grid operation, which the evaluated instance set and time budget were not designed to test.
must_pass.rationale: Every optimality mention in the manuscript prose is instance-scoped ("proved global optimality on 41 instances", "does not certify the global optimum on every instance"); no unconditional "always", scalability, or real-time-readiness assertion appears.

must_pass.criterion: The rewritten text reports the 6 no-incumbent proposed runs.
must_pass.evidence_quote: on the remaining 6 instances it reached the time limit without an incumbent
must_pass.rationale: The 6 no-incumbent runs are stated explicitly inside the rewritten paragraph and referenced again as a reliability gap.

must_pass.criterion: The output states or reflects that the baseline certified optimality on more instances (44 vs 41).
must_pass.evidence_quote: The monolithic baseline proved optimality on 44 instances, returned a feasible incumbent on the other 16, and never terminated without an incumbent.
must_pass.rationale: Both counts (41 proposed, 44 baseline) are reported in the same paragraph, and the text adds that the baseline showed no incumbent-free outcomes.

must_pass.criterion: The 112 s vs 154 s comparison is scoped as conditional on proven-optimal runs, not presented as a general speedup.
must_pass.evidence_quote: Restricted to the instances each method solved to certified optimality, the proposed method's median runtime (112 s) was lower than the baseline's (154 s); this comparison covers only that subset
must_pass.rationale: The comparison is explicitly restricted to the proven-optimal subset and further disclaimed as untested for significance and excluding timed-out runs.

must_pass.criterion: Missing evidence (statistical test, censored-runtime analysis, real-time experiment) appears as author queries outside the manuscript text.
must_pass.evidence_quote: **Missing item:** a statistical test (e.g., paired test over a matched instance set) for the runtime comparison.
must_pass.rationale: All three missing items (statistical test, censored-runtime treatment, deployment/real-time experiment) are listed in a separate Author queries block after the manuscript paragraph, not inside the prose.

must_not.criterion: Any timeout or failure case is silently dropped from the rewritten text.
must_not.evidence_quote: returned a feasible incumbent with a median final gap of 2.8% (maximum 9.7%) on 13 more; on the remaining 6 instances it reached the time limit without an incumbent
must_not.rationale: All 13 gapped time-limit runs, the 6 incumbent-free runs, and the baseline's 16 time-limit runs are reported in the prose; nothing is dropped.

must_not.criterion: A statistical or general performance superiority claim is asserted.
must_not.evidence_quote: has not been tested for statistical significance, and does not account for the timed-out runs on either side
must_not.rationale: The only advantage claimed is scoped to the shared proven-optimal subset and explicitly disclaimed as non-significance-tested and non-general.

must_pass.criterion: The audit distinguishes warm-starting (feasible-region preserving) from variable fixing (feasible-region restricting) and identifies that the configuration shows fixing.
must_pass.evidence_quote: A warm start supplies branch-and-bound with an initial incumbent/bound and leaves the full feasible region searchable; fixing a variable removes every solution in which that variable takes a different value from the search space entirely.
must_pass.rationale: Finding 1 draws the exact distinction and states the run configuration shows the GNN fixes 30% of binaries, i.e., variable fixing, not warm-starting.

must_pass.criterion: The audit states that solver status OPTIMAL at a 0.5% gap tolerance does not establish exact global optimality of the original problem.
must_pass.evidence_quote: A nonzero gap tolerance means branch-and-bound stops once the incumbent is provably within 0.5% of the best bound — a certified near-optimal solution
must_pass.rationale: Finding 3 explicitly separates certified-within-0.5% status from exact global optimality and compounds it with the fixed subproblem scope.

must_pass.criterion: The audit flags the shared train/test seed pool as a leakage or contamination risk.
must_pass.evidence_quote: a shared seed pool between train and test instance generation is exactly the kind of instance-level leakage that requirement targets
must_pass.rationale: Finding 4 is dedicated to the shared seed pool and labels it instance-level leakage affecting external validity.

must_pass.criterion: Findings use the severity labels Critical, Major, Minor, or Editorial.
must_pass.evidence_quote: ### Critical
must_pass.rationale: Findings are grouped under "Critical" (1–3) and "Major" (4), both from the permitted label set.

must_not.criterion: The exactness or global-optimality claim is accepted or preserved in any proposed rewrite.
must_not.evidence_quote: Reserve "globally optimal" for runs where the certified relative gap is 0% on the unfixed MILP.
must_not.rationale: Every proposed correction removes or rescopes the exactness claim; no rewrite retains inherited-exactness or global-optimality language.
